rules.condition: Mechanical AVR with a risk factor (AF, prior thromboembolism, LV dysfunction, hypercoagulable) or older-generation valve; or any mechanical MVR

INR 3.0 (2.5–3.5) or add aspirin 75–100 mg/day

rules.condition: New stroke on a mechanical AVR while INR therapeutic
rules.recommendation: Raise INR goal from 2.5 to 3.0 (2.5–3.5) or add aspirin 75–100 mg, weighing bleeding

rules.condition: New stroke on a mechanical MVR while INR therapeutic
rules.recommendation: Raise INR goal from 3.0 to 4.0 or add aspirin 75–100 mg, weighing bleeding

rules.condition: New stroke on a bioprosthetic valve while on antiplatelet therapy
rules.recommendation: Switching to warfarin may be considered

rules.recommendation: Long-term aspirin rather than anticoagulation
Counts as nonvalvular AF — DOAC acceptable

rules.condition: Invasive procedure: bileaflet AVR, no risk factors
rules.recommendation: Interrupt warfarin without bridging

rules.condition: Invasive procedure: AVR with a risk factor, older-generation AVR, or mechanical MVR
rules.recommendation: Bridging while INR is subtherapeutic is reasonable, individualized

rules.condition: Emergency surgery or procedure on warfarin
rules.recommendation: 4F-PCC (or aPCC) is reasonable

rules.condition: Spontaneous ICH with a mechanical valve
rules.recommendation: Early resumption of anticoagulation is reasonable

entries.title: Ischemic stroke with active cancer
keyNumbers: Possible cancer-related: cryptogenic with spread or progressing cancer plus ≥1 of D-dimer >2,500 ng/mL FEU (no VTE), multiterritory infarcts, bilateral microemboli on TCD, or no susceptibility vessel sign: Equipoise between anticoagulant and antiplatelet; decide individually
entries.question: How are acute treatment, workup and antithrombotic choice adjusted for stroke with active cancer?
population: Ischemic stroke with active cancer (diagnosis or treatment within 6 months, recurrent/advanced/metastatic, or not in remission; excludes basal/squamous skin cancer)

rules.recommendation: Use standard criteria; check CBC and coagulation studies first; review imaging for metastases
Generally defer IVT — high hemorrhage risk
Consider EVT individually, weighing goals of care and cancer prognosis (more recurrence and death than without cancer)
Add D-dimer (late in the stay if IVT/EVT given — early values falsely high), blood cultures, bubble echo or TEE, chest CT, prolonged rhythm monitoring

rules.condition: Probable cancer-related: NBTE (vegetation, negative cultures), overt DIC (ISTH ≥5), or tumor embolism
rules.recommendation: Therapeutic anticoagulation is typical — often UFH/LMWH first (especially DIC), DOAC long term; no trial data, and antiplatelets are arguable for NBTE

rules.condition: Possible cancer-related: cryptogenic with spread or progressing cancer plus ≥1 of D-dimer >2,500 ng/mL FEU (no VTE), multiterritory infarcts, bilateral microemboli on TCD, or no susceptibility vessel sign
rules.recommendation: Equipoise between anticoagulant and antiplatelet; decide individually
evidenceNote: NAVIGATE-ESUS and ARCADIA cancer subgroups neutral; TEACH and ENCHASE too small for efficacy

rules.recommendation: Treat the mechanism: DOAC for nonvalvular AF; antiplatelet + risk-factor control for small-vessel disease; usually stenting for radiation-induced carotid stenosis
Statin for most; revisit goals of care periodically; palliative care alongside cancer therapy

contraindications: Thrombocytopenia and procedure-related bleeding risk — check before anticoagulating
institutionVaries: Oncology/hematology co-management and D-dimer follow-up schedule
pearls: 1-year recurrent stroke 14–29% — 2–3× the general stroke population (Navi 2026)

Cancer-associated coagulopathy stroke: mostly within 6 months of diagnosis, advanced disease, adenocarcinoma (lung, pancreas); '3-territory sign'; 30-day mortality 25–50%; LMWH and DOACs are the most used strategies (Jauregui 2026 systematic review)
Navi 2026 follows D-dimer every few months to track treatment response
sources: Navi BB, et al. Classification and Management of Ischemic Stroke in Patients With Active Cancer: A Scientific Statement From the AHA. Stroke 2026;57:e160-e173. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000517
Jauregui Larrañaga C, et al. Stroke secondary to cancer-associated coagulopathy: a systematic review. J Neurol 2026;273:609. doi:10.1007/s00415-026-14119-y

entries.title: Stroke and antithrombotics in pregnancy and postpartum
keyNumbers: Antiplatelet needed: Aspirin <100 mg daily first choice (safe in lactation; no hold for neuraxial); clopidogrel for the shortest needed duration; ticagrelor/prasugrel minimal data
Neuraxial anesthesia timing: Aspirin: no hold; prophylactic LMWH ≥12 h; therapeutic LMWH ≥24 h; low-dose UFH 4–6 h
Enoxaparin — prophylactic: 40 mg daily (or 30 mg q12h) — fixed dosing preferred to weight-based for prophylaxis in pregnancy
Mechanical valve, warfarin >5 mg/day needed: Dose-adjusted LMWH ≥BID (anti-Xa 0.8–1.2 U/mL 4–6 h post-dose) in first trimester, then warfarin; IV UFH (aPTT 2× control) if LMWH unavailable
entries.question: Which acute treatments and antithrombotics are used in pregnancy, postpartum and lactation?
population: Pregnant or postpartum patients with stroke or a stroke-prevention indication

rules.recommendation: Don't delay standard treatment. IVT when benefit outweighs risk (alteplase and TNK don't cross the placenta; TNK data limited); individualize with planned or recent cesarean or neuraxial anesthesia
EVT as in nonpregnant patients; transradial approach preferred; consider continuous fetal monitoring in third trimester
Aspirin <100 mg daily first choice (safe in lactation; no hold for neuraxial); clopidogrel for the shortest needed duration; ticagrelor/prasugrel minimal data
LMWH first choice (safe in lactation); UFH safe; warfarin teratogenic in first trimester (select mechanical-valve cases after) and safe in lactation; DOACs — insufficient data

rules.condition: Secondary prevention after prior ischemic stroke/TIA
rules.recommendation: Low-dose aspirin for most; therapeutic LMWH for antiphospholipid syndrome, mechanical valve or prior cardioembolic stroke

rules.condition: Cryptogenic stroke with PFO, planning pregnancy
rules.recommendation: PFO closure may be considered before a future pregnancy if RoPE ≥7
Full-dose LMWH throughout pregnancy, then LMWH or VKA ≥6 weeks postpartum (≥3 months total); LMWH prophylaxis in future pregnancies
Therapeutic anticoagulation with frequent monitoring; shared decision on strategy

rules.condition: Mechanical valve, warfarin ≤5 mg/day keeps INR therapeutic
rules.recommendation: Continuing warfarin through all trimesters is reasonable after counseling
Dose-adjusted LMWH ≥BID (anti-Xa 0.8–1.2 U/mL 4–6 h post-dose) in first trimester, then warfarin; IV UFH (aPTT 2× control) if LMWH unavailable
Warfarin → BID LMWH or IV UFH ≥1 week before; LMWH → UFH ≥36 h before; stop UFH ≥6 h before vaginal delivery; labor on warfarin → cesarean after reversal
Aspirin: no hold; prophylactic LMWH ≥12 h; therapeutic LMWH ≥24 h; low-dose UFH 4–6 h

notes: Safe in lactation

1 mg/kg q12h or 1.5 mg/kg daily; mechanical valve: dose-adjust to anti-Xa 0.8–1.2 U/mL
evidenceNote: Miller 2026 Table 2; Otto 2020 for anti-Xa target

contraindications: Warfarin in the first trimester outside mechanical-valve decisions
